entities.name: Anthropic
entities.does: The Claude models

entities.name: Blue Origin
entities.does: New Shepard suborbital flights and New Glenn
notable: New Shepard has flown crew on suborbital hops since 2021
New Glenn reached orbit on its first flight, January 2025
Building the Blue Moon lunar lander for NASA's Artemis programme

entities.name: Isomorphic Labs
entities.org: Alphabet, spun out of Google DeepMind
entities.does: AlphaFold's successors, pointed at drug design instead of structure prediction.
notable: Led by Demis Hassabis, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold
Co-developed AlphaFold 3 with Google DeepMind
Drug-discovery partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies

entities.name: ISS
entities.does: Continuously crewed laboratory — microgravity science and the testbed for everything that follows
notable: Continuously crewed since November 2000
AMS-02 has been mounted outside since 2011
The testbed for every commercial crew and station programme that follows

entities.name: JWST
entities.does: Infrared astronomy — the earliest galaxies
notable: First images released July 2022
Galaxies seen further back than any telescope had reached
CO2 detected in an exoplanet atmosphere (WASP-39b), a first
The TRAPPIST-1 rocky planets, checked for air

entities.name: NIF
entities.does: 192 laser beams crush a fuel capsule until it fuses — the only laboratory on Earth to have reached ignition.
notable: December 2022: more fusion energy out than laser energy in, a first anywhere
2.05 MJ of laser light produced 3.1 MJ of fusion yield
Ignition has since been repeated at higher gain

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.does: GPT models
notable: GPT-3 (2020) then ChatGPT (2022), which moved the field into public view
The API most consumer AI products are built on

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.does: Falcon 9 and Starship launch vehicles
notable: Falcon 9: first orbital-class booster landing in 2015, now routine and reflown
Dragon: first commercial crew flight, Demo-2, in 2020
Starship: full flight tests since 2023, booster caught by the tower in 2024
Starlink: by far the largest satellite constellation ever operated
Launched Europa Clipper for NASA in October 2024

entities.name: ActInSpace
entities.status: every two years — 2026 finals in Bordeaux
entities.does: A 24-hour contest to turn a real space patent into a business idea

entities.name: AI Security Institute
entities.does: State-run evaluations of frontier models for dangerous capabilities

entities.name: AI2
entities.does: Fully open models — weights

entities.name: ALICE
entities.does: Heavy-ion collisions — the quark-gluon plasma that filled the early universe

entities.name: ALPHA
entities.does: Trapped antihydrogen — whether antimatter obeys the same spectroscopy and gravity as matter

entities.name: AMS-02
entities.does: Cosmic ray composition from space — searching for antimatter and dark matter signatures

entities.name: Arc Institute
entities.org: non-profit, with Stanford, UCSF and Berkeley
entities.does: Where AI and biology meet as one lab: genome language models built next to the wet benches that test them.
notable: Its Evo models read and write DNA across all domains of life
Used a genome language model to design working bacteriophages
Funds scientists for years at a time, not grant cycles

entities.name: Astroscale
entities.does: Rendezvous with and removal of dead satellites and debris — the orbital cleanup business
notable: ELSA-d demonstrated magnetic capture of a client satellite in 2021
ADRAS-J flew right up to a discarded Japanese rocket stage in 2024 and photographed it
Working toward actually removing debris, not just approaching it

entities.name: ATLAS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — Higgs properties and searches for new particles
notable: Co-discovered the Higgs boson in 2012
Has published thousands of measurements and searches since
Being rebuilt now for the High-Luminosity LHC

entities.name: Belle II
entities.does: Electron-positron collisions at the Upsilon(4S) — B meson decays and flavour anomalies

entities.name: BioNTech
entities.does: Founded to make cancer immunotherapy, became famous for a vaccine, and has gone back to cancer.
notable: Co-developed the first authorised mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, with Pfizer
Founders Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci started it for cancer, not viruses
Oncology pipeline now includes bispecific antibodies

entities.name: Broad Institute
entities.full_name: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
entities.does: Genomics at industrial scale, and the lab behind base editing and prime editing.
notable: Base and prime editing now in more than 25 clinical trials
gnomAD has contributed to over 13 million genetic diagnoses
Has sequenced nearly 900,000 whole human genomes

entities.name: Caltech SURF
entities.status: annual — proposals due in the winter
entities.does: A summer of research at Caltech or JPL, written up and defended like a real project — students propose the work themselves.
notable: Running since 1979
Students write their own proposal with a mentor
JPL projects are part of the same programme

entities.name: CERN Summer Student
entities.status: annual — applications close in the winter
entities.does: Eight to thirteen weeks on a real project at CERN, with a lecture series alongside it. Paid: a net allowance of 94 CHF per day, health insurance, and travel costs in some cases.
notable: For bachelor's and master's students with at least six semesters done
Physics, engineering, computer science and maths
One of the few places an undergraduate works inside a running experiment

entities.name: CMS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — the independent cross-check on ATLAS

entities.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
entities.does: A compact tokamak made possible by high-temperature superconducting magnets — the magnets are the whole bet.
notable: SPARC is designed to be the first commercially relevant machine to produce net fusion energy
ARC, the power plant meant to follow it, is already sited
The largest private fusion company by funding

entities.name: Copernicus Masters
entities.does: Prizes

entities.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
entities.does: Makes the first approved CRISPR medicine: patients' own stem cells, edited and returned.
notable: Casgevy, developed with Vertex, is approved for sickle cell disease and beta thalassaemia
Co-founded by Emmanuelle Charpentier
The first time gene editing became a prescription

entities.name: DESY Summer Students
entities.does: Seven and a half weeks inside a major accelerator laboratory, on photon science, accelerators, particle or astroparticle physics.
notable: 2026 edition ran 21 July to 10 September
Free hostel accommodation plus a daily stipend, travel partly reimbursed
Open to undergraduates in physics and related fields

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.does: Grassroots open-source research collective; released open models when almost nobody else did

entities.name: ESA Business Incubation
entities.does: Funding

entities.name: ESA Young Graduate Trainee
entities.does: About 100 one-year paid traineeships a year for people finishing a master's degree

entities.name: Euclid
entities.does: Surveying a third of the sky to map how dark energy stretched the universe
notable: First survey images, November 2023
First bulk data release, 2025 — the survey is meant to run six years

entities.name: Europa Clipper
entities.does: Will fly close passes over Europa to test whether its subsurface ocean could be habitable
notable: Launched October 2024 on a Falcon Heavy
Mars gravity assist, March 2025
Will make dozens of close passes rather than orbit Europa — radiation would kill it

entities.name: Exotrail
entities.does: Electric thrusters and an orbital transfer vehicle — the tow truck that moves satellites
notable: spacevan, an orbital transfer vehicle, has flown
ExoMG Hall thrusters fly on other operators' smallsats
Sells the manoeuvre, not the hardware — mobility as a service

entities.name: FASER
entities.does: Very forward particles — collider neutrinos and long-lived light particles

entities.name: Fervo Energy
entities.does: Geothermal power anywhere hot rock is deep enough, using the horizontal drilling and fibre sensing the oil industry perfected.
notable: Signed a 396 MW power purchase agreement with Google, September 2026
Building Cape Station in Utah
Staffed deliberately with oil and gas engineers

entities.name: Firefly Aerospace
entities.does: Alpha launch vehicle and the Blue Ghost lunar lander
notable: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed upright on Mare Crisium in March 2025
Alpha is its small launch vehicle
One of the few commercial landers to reach the Moon intact

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.does: Gemini
notable: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016
AlphaFold predicted protein structures at scale; its authors shared a Nobel in 2024
Gemini is the production model line

entities.name: Google Summer of Code
entities.does: Twelve weeks contributing to an open-source project with a mentor from that project, stipend included. Several scientific-software organisations take part each year.
notable: Over 21,000 contributors since 2005, across 1,000+ organisations
Astropy, the HEP software projects and similar groups participate regularly
Contact the organisation before the proposal window — that is what decides selection

entities.name: Helion
entities.does: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion that aims to turn the plasma's energy straight into electricity, skipping the steam turbine.
notable: Polaris: the first privately built machine to show measurable deuterium-tritium fusion
Raised $465 million in June 2026 at a $15.5 billion valuation
Building Orion, which it calls the first fusion power plant

entities.name: Hubble
entities.does: Optical and ultraviolet astronomy — still the sharpest UV eye we have
notable: The Deep Field (1995): point at nothing, find thousands of galaxies
Pinned down the expansion rate, and started the tension over its value
Still working after 35 years and five servicing missions

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.does: The public hub where models and datasets are shared — the field's distribution layer

entities.name: IAI Space
entities.does: Observation and communications satellites
notable: Ofek reconnaissance satellites, launched on Israel's own Shavit rocket
The Amos communications satellite series
Built the Beresheet lander with SpaceIL
One of about eleven organisations worldwide with end-to-end space capability

entities.name: IceCube
entities.does: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos
notable: Found the first high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, 2013
Traced one 2017 event back to a flaring blazar
Mapped neutrino emission from the plane of our own galaxy, 2023

entities.name: ICEYE
entities.does: Small radar satellites that image through cloud and darkness
notable: Put the first smallsat synthetic-aperture radar in orbit
Its flood maps are used by insurers and disaster response
Radar sees through cloud and at night, which optical imaging cannot

entities.name: ICTP Trieste
entities.full_name: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics
entities.does: Schools, workshops and a diploma year in theoretical physics, aimed particularly at scientists from countries without that training at home.
notable: Founded by Abdus Salam to keep physics from concentrating in rich countries
Most schools cover travel and accommodation for accepted participants
Work here fed into neutrino oscillation theory and climate modelling

entities.name: ImageSat International
entities.does: High-resolution observation satellites and the analysis layer on top of them
notable: Operates the EROS high-resolution observation satellites
GEOIMPACT layers AI analysis over the imagery
Sells sovereign capability, not only pictures

entities.name: Intuitive Machines
entities.does: Nova-C lunar landers flown under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme
notable: IM-1 Odysseus, February 2024 — the first US soft landing since Apollo, though it tipped over
IM-2 Athena followed in March 2025
Flies under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme

entities.name: JUICE
entities.does: Will study Ganymede
notable: Launched April 2023
First ever Moon-then-Earth double gravity assist, August 2024
Venus flyby 2025; Jupiter arrival planned 2031

entities.name: KATRIN
entities.does: The neutrino mass directly

entities.name: LHCb
entities.does: Beauty and charm quark decays — matter/antimatter asymmetry and flavour anomalies

entities.name: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
entities.does: Spacetime ripples from merging black holes and neutron stars
notable: GW150914 (2015): the first direct detection, two black holes merging
GW170817 (2017): a neutron star merger seen in gravitational waves and in light
The O4 observing run has pushed the catalogue past 200 candidate events

entities.name: LZ
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — XENONnT's main competitor and cross-check

entities.name: Meta FAIR
entities.does: Open-weight Llama models and a large share of the field's published research

entities.name: Mila
entities.does: One of the largest academic deep learning groups

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.does: Europe's frontier lab

entities.name: Moderna
entities.does: Medicines written as mRNA: instructions the body's own cells follow to make the protein that does the work.
notable: COVID-19 vaccine, 2020
Its mRNA flu vaccine was approved by the FDA in August 2026
Personalised cancer vaccines built from each patient's tumour are in late-stage trials

entities.name: NA62
entities.does: The ultra-rare kaon decay K+ to pi+ nu nubar — one of the sharpest tests of the Standard Model

entities.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
entities.does: A weekend hackathon on real agency data; local events run in Israel and across Europe

entities.name: Oxford PV
entities.org: private, spun out of Oxford University
entities.does: Perovskite layered on silicon — two cells in one, each catching the part of sunlight the other wastes.
notable: Built on Henry Snaith's perovskite research
Among the first to put perovskite-silicon tandems into commercial modules
Tandems are how solar gets past the single-junction efficiency limit

entities.name: Parker Solar Probe
entities.does: Flying through the Sun's corona to find out what heats it and accelerates the solar wind
notable: First spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona, 2021
Closest approach December 2024, about 6.1 million km from the surface
Fastest object ever built by humans

entities.name: Perseverance
entities.does: Roving an ancient river delta and caching samples for a future return mission
notable: Carried Ingenuity, which flew 72 times before its rotor was damaged in 2024
Sample tubes cached at Three Forks, waiting for a return mission
Found organic molecules in Jezero's delta rocks

entities.name: Pierre Auger Observatory
entities.does: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays — where the most energetic particles in nature come from

entities.name: Planet Labs
entities.does: Images the entire landmass of Earth daily with a fleet of small optical satellites
notable: The Dove flock images Earth's entire landmass daily
SkySat adds high-resolution tasking on top of that baseline
Archive now spans more than a decade of daily coverage

entities.name: Ramon Foundation
entities.does: Israel's space education pipeline — school programmes

entities.name: Ramon.Space
entities.does: Radiation-tolerant computers for spacecraft — supercomputing that survives orbit
notable: Radiation-tolerant processors that keep working through orbital radiation
Aimed at moving real computation off the ground and into the spacecraft
Opened US engineering operations near Denver

entities.name: Rocket Lab
entities.does: Electron small launcher
notable: Electron reached orbit in 2018 and is the busiest small launcher
Launched CAPSTONE to lunar orbit for NASA in 2022
Recovers boosters from the sea to study reuse
Neutron, a larger reusable vehicle, is in development

entities.name: Rubin Observatory
entities.does: Will image the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
notable: First-look images released June 2025
Will repeat the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
Expected to multiply the number of known solar system objects

entities.name: SolarEdge
entities.does: The electronics between a solar panel and the grid — optimisers and inverters that get more out of every roof.
notable: Installed in more than 140 countries
Leads in rooftop solar capacity
Moved into home storage and grid services

entities.name: StemRad
entities.does: The AstroRad vest
notable: AstroRad flew on Artemis I around the Moon, on the MARE experiment
Also tested aboard the ISS
Shields bone marrow selectively rather than the whole body

entities.name: StoreDot
entities.does: Silicon-anode batteries built to charge an electric car in minutes rather than hours.
notable: Extreme-fast-charging cells at 300 Wh/kg
Partnerships with Mercedes, Volvo and Polestar
Backed by bp and TDK

entities.name: T2K
entities.does: Neutrino oscillation and hints of CP violation in the lepton sector

entities.name: TerraPower
entities.does: Natrium, a sodium-cooled fission reactor with molten-salt storage bolted on — so the plant can surge when the grid needs it.
notable: First plant under construction in Wyoming
345 MWe, with over five hours of molten-salt energy storage
Also developing medical isotopes for cancer treatment

entities.name: Voyager 1 and 2
entities.does: The only working instruments humanity has outside the Sun's bubble
notable: Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018
Engineers recovered Voyager 1 from a failed memory chip in 2024, from 24 billion km away
Instruments are being switched off one by one to stretch the power budget

entities.name: Weizmann Institute
entities.does: One of the world's leading basic-science institutes, strong in immunology, cancer and the gut microbiome.
notable: Its ILLUMINE team won up to £20m in Cancer Grand Challenges, 2025
Pioneering work linking gut microbes to immunity
Research here led to several of Israel's best-known drugs

entities.name: Wendelstein 7-X
entities.org: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics
entities.does: The largest stellarator ever built — a twisted magnetic bottle designed to hold plasma continuously rather than in pulses.
notable: First plasma in December 2015; 50 superconducting coils, none of them a simple shape
Built to sustain discharges up to 30 minutes
Reaches confinement comparable to tokamaks without their pulsed limit

entities.name: XENONnT
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — a WIMP recoiling off a liquid xenon nucleus

entities.name: XRISM
entities.does: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy — the motion of hot gas around black holes and clusters
notable: Resolve spectrometer reads gas motion around black holes to a few km/s
First science results released 2024

canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor
canon.why: How hot, how dense and for how long — the bar every fusion machine is still measured against.

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
canon.why: One page, and the double helix. Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, which she was not told they had.

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
canon.why: Quantum mechanics turned into the chemist's everyday picture of bonds and hybrid orbitals.

canon.title: A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae
canon.why: Two and a half pages showing the universe is expanding. Cosmology starts here.

watch.name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
watch.why: Nine lectures building a working GPT from nothing, in code, with every line explained.

watch.name: Neural networks
watch.why: The visual explanation of what a network is actually doing. Start here if the maths looks opaque.

watch.name: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
watch.why: Top-down: you train a working model in lesson one and learn why it worked afterwards.

watch.name: Short courses (agents, RAG, evaluation)
watch.why: Short, current, built with the labs themselves — though the catalogue has moved to a membership.

watch.name: Paper walkthroughs
watch.why: Reads the week's papers out loud and argues with them, which is how you learn to read them yourself.

watch.name: PBS Space Time
watch.why: The rare channel that keeps the real equations in and still stays followable.

watch.name: Dr. Becky
watch.why: A working astrophysicist walking through the month's results, including the ones that did not hold up.

watch.name: Fermilab
watch.why: Particle physics explained by the lab that does it, without the press-release gloss.

watch.name: Cool Worlds
watch.why: A working exoplanet astronomer thinking out loud about habitability and how we would ever know.

watch.name: Anton Petrov
watch.why: A short, careful video on almost every new astronomy result, usually within days of the paper.

watch.name: Kurzgesagt
watch.why: The most beautiful science animation being made, and the sources are published alongside each video.

watch.name: Deep Sky Videos
watch.why: Real astronomers talking through objects one at a time, telescope time included.

watch.name: Event Horizon
watch.why: Long interviews with the researchers themselves — where cosmology arguments actually get made.

watch.name: Scott Manley
watch.why: Orbital mechanics and launch failures explained by someone who reads the telemetry.

watch.name: Astrum
watch.why: Built from real probe imagery — what the spacecraft actually sent back, not an artist's impression.

books.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
books.who: Gelman, Carlin, Stern, Dunson, Vehtari and Rubin
books.why: How to reason about uncertainty when you have a model and not much data. Free PDF from the authors.

books.title: Numerical Recipes
books.why: The algorithms behind the library functions you call, explained well enough to know when they will fail you.

books.title: Statistical Data Analysis
books.why: The standard reference for how physicists actually handle errors, fits and limits. Short, and nothing wasted.

books.title: Data Reduction and Error Analysis for the Physical Sciences
books.why: The first statistics book most physics students meet, and the one they keep going back to.

books.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
books.why: If you are going to publish plots, read this before you publish more of them.

books.title: An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics
books.why: The standard undergraduate course in one very heavy volume — stars, galaxies, cosmology, all of it.

books.title: Introduction to Cosmology
books.why: The clearest first cosmology book there is. You can read it end to end without getting stuck.

books.title: Black Holes and Time Warps
books.why: Written before LIGO detected anything, by the person who argued it would. Worth reading for that alone.

books.title: The First Three Minutes
books.why: A Nobel laureate walking through the early universe minute by minute, without hiding the physics.

books.title: Liftoff
books.why: How SpaceX nearly died before Falcon 1 reached orbit. Reported, not mythologised.

books.title: Reentry
books.why: The sequel: Falcon 9, reuse, and the decisions that turned a survivor into the whole market.

books.title: Space Mission Analysis and Design
books.why: The engineering reference the industry actually sizes missions with. Known simply as SMAD.

books.title: The Right Stuff
books.why: Why anyone climbs onto a rocket at all. Still the best writing about test pilots and nerve.

books.title: Modern Particle Physics
books.why: The current standard course. Works the calculations through instead of quoting results.

books.title: Introduction to Elementary Particles
books.why: Griffiths explains things the way a good supervisor would. Start here before Thomson.

books.title: Review of Particle Physics
books.why: Every measured property of every known particle, updated yearly and free. The field's single most-used document.

books.title: Lost in Math
books.why: An argument that beauty has been a bad guide in theoretical physics. Contested, and worth arguing with.

books.title: Plasma Physics and Fusion Energy
books.why: What it would actually take to build a fusion reactor, with the engineering constraints left in.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.why: A Pulitzer for a book that is also a genuine history of 20th-century nuclear physics. Read it for Meitner and Bohr.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.why: Reactor physics as it behaves when institutions fail. The clearest account of what actually happened.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.why: The foundations, from linear algebra up. Free online, and still the reference for why things work.

books.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
books.why: Bridges classical statistics and deep learning in one framework. Draft PDF free, code in Python and JAX.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.why: By the people who built the field. Free PDF, and still the clearest treatment of the basics.

books.title: The Alignment Problem
books.why: The honest version of why making these systems do what we meant is hard, told through the research.

books.title: Sustainable Energy — Without the Hot Air
books.why: Every energy argument turned into kilowatt-hours per person per day. Free online, and it settles a lot of arguments.

books.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell
books.why: The textbook of cell biology. If you come from physics, this is where the vocabulary comes from.

books.title: The Gene
books.why: From Mendel to gene editing, written by an oncologist with a family history that makes it personal.

books.title: The Code Breaker
books.why: Jennifer Doudna and the race to CRISPR, with the rivalries left in.

books.title: The Emperor of All Maladies
books.why: A biography of cancer. Won the Pulitzer, and explains why the mRNA cancer vaccines matter so much.

items.abstract: Recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed fine-structure lines of ions with ionization potentials ${\gtrsim}50$\,eV, such as [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [O\,{\sc iv}], in nebular spectra of some low-metallicity galaxies, raising questions about the nature of the ionizing sources. Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) have been considered as potential contributors, but direct evidence linking individual ULXs to highly ionized nebulae is limited. Here we present JWST IFU spectroscopy of the nebula surrounding the template ULX Ho\,II\,X--1 in the low-metallicity galaxy Holmberg\,II, already known to emit He\,{\sc ii}\,$\lambda4686$ and [O\,{\sc iv}]\,25.89\,$μ$m lines. We resolve the infrared nebula on spatial scales of ${\sim}15-25$\,pc and report the first detections of [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [Ne\,{\sc vi}] in this source. We find anisotropic ionizing conditions: emission from the highest-ionization species arises from compact regions offset from the ULX toward the previously detected radio knots, whereas lower-ionization species trace the wider nebula. The preferential alignment of the highest-ionization emission with the radio axis suggests anisotropic escape of the ionizing continuum and a physical connection with jet-ejection activity. Spectral lines across the nebula are narrow and consistent with the instrumental resolution, indicating kinematically quiescent gas and disfavoring shocks as the dominant ionization mechanism. Together, these results provide direct evidence linking an individual ULX to a highly ionized nebula in a low-metallicity galaxy. These JWST observations of Ho~II~X--1 show that an accreting black hole in a low-metallicity galaxy is responsible for the extreme ionization of the surrounding nebula on ${\sim}100$\,pc scales.

items.title: A spatial map of the atmospheric limb of a hot Jupiter
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. Here we apply the novel transmission strings mapping method to the hot Jupiter WASP-17 b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can also map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6–12 μm. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with an approximately 650 K temperature difference between the morning ( $$85{8}_{-233}^{+434}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 85 8 − 233 + 434 K ) and evening $$1{,}52{2}_{-114}^{+116}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 1 , 52 2 − 114 + 116 K ). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H 2 O and CO 2 to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints for results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique, combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17 b, pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry.

items.title: Probing fundamental physics with ALMA2040 mm-wavelength observations of neutron stars
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Bursty or (rotation-induced) pulsed coherent radio emission from pulsars, magnetars, and fast radio transients originates in some of the most extreme environments in the Universe. However, the exact physical mechanism behind the scenes remains poorly understood. ALMA2040 will allow for systematic exploration of the millimeter-wavelength spectral window for pulsars and fast radio transients for the very first time, offering unprecedented opportunities to discover new observational phenomena and advance our understanding of emission physics. Beyond this, ALMA2040 provides a unique means to unveil the neutron-star population in the Galactic Centre (GC), enable novel tests of fundamental physics in the vicinity of the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, probe the potential existence of dark matter in the GC, and investigate the dense, highly dynamic interstellar and magnetic environment of this region.

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Rings are ubiquitous among the giant planets in the Solar System, yet their presence around exoplanets remains observationally unconstrained. As direct imaging missions such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope approach first light, understanding the influence of circumplanetary rings on reflected light photometry is critical for the accurate interpretation and follow-up of direct imaging observations. We present a hybrid forward model for reflected light phase curves of ringed exoplanets, coupling a ray casting framework for computing mutual planet-ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings. We model Jupiter-like planets with opaque, icy rings spanning 1 - 10x the radial extent of Saturn's A, B, and C rings across a grid of inclinations and ring obliquities. Our simulations show that rings enhance the flux ratios at favorable ring geometries. Saturn-equivalent rings increase peak flux by a factor of 3.1 in the visible, while more extended rings produce enhanced contrasts exceeding an order of magnitude more. The flux contribution of a ring is highly sensitive to obliquity and orbital location. At certain geometries, rings can suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. We highlight multi-band observations as a complementary route for diagnosing the presence of an exoring. We also apply the model to $\upsilon$ Andromedae d as an observational test case and discuss the implications for exoring detectability with the Roman Coronagraph. Exorings have the potential to bias inferred planetary properties from direct images and must be properly accounted for in observation preparation and interpretation.

items.title: The Atmospheric Chemistry and Surface Interactions on Mars (ACSIOM) Workshop 2025
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The ACSIOM workshop was held in Cambridge from 10th-12th November 2025. Its primary aims were twofold: 1) to gather UK researchers involved in Mars atmospheric science to identify current shortcomings and challenges in the field, and 2) to discuss possible collaborations and future steps needed to maximise the research output from current and future Mars missions. Workshop attendees spanned a wide range of subjects and disciplines, from atmospheric modellers and surface scientists to experimental chemists and Earth/Venus/exoplanet scientists. One of the primary outcomes of the workshop as identified by the attendees was the need for more collaborations between these different communities. It was agreed that we currently lack sufficient interaction between disciplines and this is a key challenge we need to overcome in order to properly utilise and exploit the vast pool of martian expertise available in the UK. Modellers need reaction rates from experimentalists; experimentalists need modelling context to prioritise their experiments; geologists need modelling context to understand the features they see; modellers need geological context to constrain their results. Attendees stressed that the UK Mars community has a critical mass which is internationally recognised, and improving the communication between communities would allow significant progress to be made in martian research, allowing the UK to maintain leadership in Mars science for years to come. We highlight that this is a pivotal moment for such investments as many planetary missions, both for Mars and other terrestrial bodies, are about to be launched or are being considered in the coming years. Having a strong and close-knit community will be key to better identifying needs and capabilities in order to optimise investments in missions and to have the best scientific return possible.

items.title: Measurement of Born cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.5-4.9 GeV and partial wave analysis at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 44.6 $\rm fb^{-1}$, we present the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. By fitting the dressed cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. with the assumption of a power-law function plus a charmonium(-like) resonance, i.e., $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$, $ψ(4160)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $ψ(4415)$, $ψ(4500)$, $Y(4660)$ or $ψ(4710)$, no significant charmonium(-like) state decaying into $pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. is observed. The product of branching fractions and electronic partial widths including their upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are provided for each decay. In addition, a partial wave analysis of the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV is performed to investigate $N^{*}$, $Λ^{*}$ and $Σ^{*}$ resonances in the $K^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ and $pK^{-}$ invariant mass spectra. Significant contributions are found from the $Λ(1520)$, $Σ(1670)$, $Σ(1915)$, $N(1900)$, $N(2300)$ and $N(2570)$. The masses, widths and production fractions for each component are determined.

items.title: Improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response in athermal phonon detectors: implications for quasiparticle dynamics
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Our detectors for Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino--Nucleus Scattering (CE$ν$NS) use photolithographically patterned superconducting athermal phonon sensors that are coupled to kg-scale absorbers of different materials (germanium, silicon, sapphire). Following a particle interaction, athermal phonons from the bulk absorber break Cooper pairs in a superconducting aluminum film that surrounds a tungsten Transition Edge Sensor (TES) in equilibrium through electrothermal feedback. This sensor design is called Quasiparticle-trap-assisted Electro-thermal-feedback Transition-edge-sensor (QET). The QET aluminum film that absorbs the athermal phonons is patterned into fins with lengths limited by the quasiparticle diffusion length in aluminum. Improving the quasiparticle diffusion length in the superconducting aluminum is an area of vigorous research to improve phonon collection efficiency and increase the signal strength for lower-threshold searches. We report significantly improved aluminum films that show systematically larger grain sizes and residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) compared to detectors we have fabricated in the past. The improved RRR and grain sizes were expected to improve the collected signal for a given energy. We report higher signal strength achieved in a detector in comparison to another detector in which all other fabrication parameters were kept identical except for the aluminum film deposition.

items.title: Cryogenic characterisation of the FBK NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers for the DarkSide-20k dark matter experiment
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are highly promising detectors for dark matter searches due to their uniform response, scalability to large target masses, and compatibility with ultra-low background conditions. The DarkSide-20k (DS-20k) experiment, currently under construction at Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare (INFN) Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), aims to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), approaching the neutrino fog. At the heart of the detector is a dual-phase TPC filled and surrounded by low-radioactivity argon from underground sources (i.e. Underground Argon (UAr)), functioning both as the WIMP target and detection medium. The experiment employs Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) as the chosen photon sensors for its optical planes. Key SiPM properties such as dark noise rate, gain and direct crosstalk were measured using specialized test setups at 77 K. The photon detection efficiency (PDE) was measured under vacuum at 77 K over the wavelength range 350-820 nm. Secondary photon emission, which can give rise to external optical crosstalk, was measured under vacuum at 86 K over the wavelength range 550-1020 nm.

items.title: Two families of multi-planet systems with distinct architectures and stellar hosts
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The rapidly growing census of exoplanets now includes over a thousand multi-planet systems, revealing architectures that span more than four orders of magnitude in mass and five in orbital scale. Explaining the origin of this striking diversity remains a central challenge for planet formation theory, compounded by observational biases that limit access to Solar System-like regimes. Here we introduce architecture-agnostic metrics to uniformly analyse four independently defined samples of multi-planet systems, uncovering unifying patterns across their diversity. We identify a clear bimodality in system masses, dividing known architectures into two distinct families. The lower-mass family, predominantly hosted by subsolar-to-solar stars, exhibits tightly packed configurations with mass distributions consistent with the ‘peas-in-a-pod’ pattern and modal dynamical excitation comparable with that of the Solar System. By contrast, the high-mass family forms in metal-rich environments around solar-to-supersolar stars, displays gravitationally compact architectures and is an order of magnitude dynamically hotter than both the Solar System and the lower-mass counterparts. Their high level of dynamical excitation points to violent evolutionary pathways driven by global instabilities and planet–planet scattering. Together, these results show that the architectures of planetary systems are born from the combined influence of formation processes and host star properties. Signatures of these roots are preserved across the post-formation dynamical evolution that reshaped most known multi-planet systems.

items.title: Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: In conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors, the transition temperature and the linear-in-temperature normal-state scattering rate are linked through the electron–phonon coupling strength. In cuprate high-temperature superconductors, no equivalent relationship between critical temperature and electron–boson coupling has been identified. Here we highlight such a link with electrons scattering off commensurate antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations of variable strength. We use d.c. resistivity and high-field magnetoresistance to extract the scattering rate in electron-doped La 2− x Ce x CuO 4 as a function of doping. We reveal a highly anisotropic inelastic component to the scattering rate whose magnitude diminishes markedly as doping increases. The correlation we highlight between the strength of scattering and the critical temperature then identifies low-energy spin fluctuations as the primary pairing glue in electron-doped cuprates. The contrasting magnetotransport behaviour in hole-doped cuprates suggests that the higher critical temperature in those materials cannot be attributed solely to an increase in the coupling strength to the antiferromagnetic fluctuations. The success in modelling La 2− x Ce x CuO 4 reinforces the notion that resolving the origin of high-temperature superconductivity in hole-doped cuprates may require more than a simple extension of the Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer theory.

items.title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh 2 ( R -3,5- di PheTPCP) 4 features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

items.title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

items.title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

items.title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

items.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising path to scalable quantum computing due to their compatibility with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. A key requirement for scaling quantum processors is the ability to perform high-fidelity operations in parallel across many qubits. However, simultaneous control remains a major challenge in silicon devices, as fidelities typically degrade under parallel operation. Here we identify microwave-drive-induced a.c.-Stark shifts as the dominant source of this degradation in a five-qubit silicon spin array. We address this by introducing a scalable mitigation protocol based solely on pairwise phase calibrations. Using tailored control pulses on a shared control line, we achieve primitive X and Y gate fidelities well above 99.99% for each qubit individually, with some approaching 99.999%. Furthermore, these fidelities are preserved above 99.99% during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits. During parallel five-qubit operation, fidelities remain above the widely targeted fault-tolerant threshold of 99.9%. By maintaining high-fidelity control during simultaneous operation, shared qubit-control lines can support the development of large-scale semiconductor quantum processors.

items.title: Time-Dependent Wave-Packet Approach to Reactions for Quantum Computation
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: We describe a method for obtaining the scattering matrix for nuclear or chemical reactions on a finite lattice. Aside from the preparation of the initial and final states as wave packets, the only other operation required is unitary time evolution, making this approach ideal for simulations on quantum hardware. The central quantity is a time-dependent overlap between incoming and outgoing wave packets whose Fourier transform corresponds to the scattering matrix at fixed energy, from which one can calculate elastic and inelastic cross sections for reactions involving two interacting clusters. Working in Cartesian coordinates enables an efficient encoding of the problem on quantum hardware via the first quantization mapping, with favorable qubit scaling for describing asymptotic scattering states. Within this framework, we describe a quantum algorithm for probing the scattering amplitude through different angles, including the forward direction, which provides access to the total cross section via the optical theorem. We demonstrate our methods through a series of numerical examples, for both elastic and inelastic processes, comparing against exact calculations. The techniques we describe can more readily be extended to a large number of constituent particles than other existing approaches, once fault-tolerant quantum hardware becomes available.

items.title: Reactor Antineutrino Detection with JUNO-TAO: Commissioning Performance and First Results
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory (TAO) is a satellite experiment of JUNO, designed to measure the reactor antineutrino energy spectrum with high precision at a baseline of 43.2~m from a reactor core using a 2.8-ton spherical liquid-scintillator detector, 1.8~m in diameter, operated at -50 degree and instrumented with 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles. The TAO detector installation was completed in 2025, and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. This paper reports the detector design, calibration strategy, and performance based on commissioning data and the first physics runs. Stable cryogenic operation has been achieved, and about 90\% of the readout channels are retained for physics analysis after channel-quality selections. The detector light yield is measured to be about 4000~photoelectrons/MeV after correction for dark noise and optical crosstalk, using neutron capture on hydrogen in inverse beta decay (IBD) events. The energy resolution is about 2.8\% for \(^{68}\)Ge at the detector center and about 3.7\% for \(^{137}\)Cs at \(R=193\)~mm. This energy-resolution performance is among the best reported for reactor-antineutrino detectors and enables TAO to measure the reactor antineutrino spectrum with high precision. Within the fiducial volume of \(R < 800\)~mm, the vertex reconstruction bias remains within \(\pm 30~\mathrm{mm}\), and the resolution is approximately \(70~\mathrm{mm}\) over most of the fiducial volume. The combined muon-tagging efficiency of the veto system is about 97\%. Using 31.3 days of reactor-on data and 29.4 days of reactor-off data, a significant excess of IBD candidates is observed in the reactor-on sample relative to the reactor-off sample, with candidate rates of 2900$\pm$10 events/day and 419$\pm$4 events/day, respectively. The results demonstrate that TAO has reached a high performance level in reactor antineutrino measurement.

items.title: A modern particle-in-cell code for beam-beam simulations of future colliders
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: A key challenge in the design of next-generation colliders is predicting the effects of beam-beam interactions and using these predictions to optimize machine performance. Beam-beam interactions are characterized by strong focusing forces, radiative effects, and the generation of background particles. While analytical formulas provide insight into the dynamics of beam-beam interactions, these nonlinear, coupled effects are most accurately described with numerical methods. In this paper, we introduce the open-source particle-in-cell code WarpX as a modern tool for modeling the interaction point in future lepton colliders. WarpX provides high-performance execution on distributed GPU architectures within an open-source and actively maintained code base. We present convergence scans and benchmarks against the established beam-beam codes GUINEA-PIG (v1.2.2) and CAIN (v2.42) for luminosity spectra, photon emission, and secondary-particle production under a wide range of beam parameters corresponding to different collider concepts. Our results show that WarpX (v26.09) reproduces the benchmark beam-beam observables while enabling GPU-portable, extensible simulations. These results establish WarpX as a scalable platform for high-fidelity beam-beam modeling in future collider studies.

items.title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

items.title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The ciliary transition zone (TZ) regulates ciliary proteome composition, yet its molecular architecture, protein content, and contribution to motile ciliopathies remain poorly defined. We applied in situ cryo–electron tomography and subtomogram averaging to human multiciliated epithelial cells. This approach resolved TZ-specific doublet microtubules at subnanometer resolution and identified nine constituent proteins. We found that epithelial cell transforming 2 like (ECT2L) and double zinc ribbon and ankyrin repeat-containing protein 1 (DZANK1) form the major linker complexes between adjacent TZ doublet microtubules. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in either gene cause primary ciliary dyskinesia. ECT2L and DZANK1 deficiency disrupted TZ architecture, caused microtubular abnormalities and abnormal bulbous ciliary tips, and impaired mucociliary clearance. These findings establish a direct genetic link between TZ defects and human motile ciliopathy and illustrate how in situ structural biology can uncover mechanisms of human disease.

items.title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

items.title: Real-Time String Dynamics in a <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> <mml:mrow> <mml:mn>2</mml:mn> <mml:mo>+</mml:mo> <mml:mn>1</mml:mn> <mml:mi mathvariant="normal">D</mml:mi> </mml:mrow> </mml:math> Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: String Breaking, Glueball Formation, Baryon Blockade, and Tension Reduction
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Understanding flux string dynamics can provide insight into quark confinement and hadronization. First-principles quantum and numerical simulations have mostly focused on toy-model Abelian lattice gauge theories (LGTs). With the advent of state-of-the-art quantum simulation experiments, it is timely to study string dynamics in non-Abelian LGTs beyond one spatial dimension. Using tensor network methods, we simulate the real-time string dynamics of a 2 + 1 D SU(2) Yang-Mills LGT with dynamical matter. In the strong-coupling regime and at resonance, string breaking occurs via a sharp Casimir reduction, along with meson and baryon-antibaryon formation, a distinctively non-Abelian feature. At finite baryon density, we discover a mechanism that delays string breaking. Away from resonance, the magnetic term drives purely non-Abelian fluctuations: glueball-like excitations and self-crossed strings that resolve two SU(2) intertwiners with distinct dynamics. For higher-energy strings, we uncover representation-dependent tension-reduction resonances. Our findings serve as a guide for upcoming quantum simulators of non-Abelian LGTs.

items.title: Precision Hypernuclear Structure from Interaction Cross Sections
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: We establish interaction cross sections as a quantitative structural observable for hypernuclei. Using the hypertriton, H Λ 3 , as the most stringent benchmark, microscopic three-body wave functions are combined with a finite-range coupled-channel Glauber calculation and Bayesian inversion. For H Λ 3 + C 12 at 1.5 GeV / nucleon , the interaction cross section decreases from about 1150 to 750 mb as the Λ separation energy B Λ increases from 0.1 to 0.5 MeV, while propagated reaction-model uncertainties remain near 5%. A measurement therefore supplies a direct inversion σ I → r m → B Λ , constraining both the matter radius and the Λ separation energy. The framework provides the missing quantitative link between proposed interaction-cross-section measurements and the spatial structure of an already formed hypernucleus. Although demonstrated for the hypertriton, the methodology is readily extendable to other weakly bound hypernuclei.

items.abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces require reliable decoding from multichannel EEG, but practical acquisition often yields sparse or corrupted electrode montages. We propose TriRouter, an electrode-space routing framework with discriminative-preservation, mask-robustness, and latent-compensation paths. A validation-calibrated router uses observable channel availability to allocate path contributions, preserving complete-channel discrimination while increasing representation recovery under severe missingness. In BNCI2014-001, TriRouter outperforms standard public backbones and a dynamic-spatial-filtering corrupted-EEG baseline. It improves accuracy over the strongest corrupted-EEG baseline by 3.68, 4.02, and 6.46 percentage points at nominal 25%, 50%, and 75% missing settings, and remains effective under structured regional missingness and additional low-channel dataset evaluation.

items.title: Machine-learning-based neutrino-event generation constrained by experimental measurements
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We present a generative surrogate for charged-current \(ν_μ\)-nucleus scattering that can be calibrated to measured differential cross sections without event-level experimental samples. Starting from a theoretical interaction model, we fine-tune the surrogate to a MicroBooNE measurement and show that this also improves the description of observables not used in the fit. The calibrated model can also be applied to measurements from different neutrino fluxes without retuning, while retaining event-level predictions of outgoing-muon kinematics. Our results show that experimental cross sections can directly constrain generative event models while preserving their applicability across different observables and beam configurations.

items.title: Harness-Driven Agentic Operation of Optical Pooled Screen Analysis
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Optical pooled screens connect genetic perturbations to changes in cell morphology and behavior, but turning the microscopy data into interpretable results takes complex, multi-day analyses. Established pipelines process this data, yet researchers still select parameters, inspect outputs, and resolve failures for each experiment. Here, we present Brieflow-auto, a pipeline-specific harness implemented as a Claude Code plugin that lets a coding large language model (LLM) operate Brieflow, an open-source end-to-end pipeline for optical pooled screening data. A researcher supplies experimental facts and approves the launch. An agent tunes parameters in an interactive notebook, and the harness validates the configuration, monitors execution, recovers from common failures, and checks output quality. For pipeline defects, the agent opens upstream issues proposing backward-compatible fixes for the broader community. In five previously analyzed screens, harness runs yielded more cells with a confident single-gene assignment than the original hand analyses. On a screen the pipeline was not designed for, the harness turned each failure into a reviewed upstream fix. More broadly, we propose that wrapping an established pipeline in a harness can substantially accelerate its use and the long-term reliability of its codebase.

items.title: Syntaxin11 deficiency inhibits CRAC channel priming to suppress cytotoxicity and gene expression in T lymphocytes independent of membrane trafficking
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Mutations in Syntaxin11 (STX11), a Q-SNARE, result in a fatal immune disorder known as familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis 4 (FHLH4) in human patients. A key diagnostic feature of FHLH4 is defective T and natural killer cell cytotoxicity. Here, we show that STX11 directly binds and regulates Orai1, the pore-forming subunit of calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channels. CRAC channels enable store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) from the extracellular space and are crucial for granule exocytosis and nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT)-dependent gene expression in activated lymphocytes. STX11 depletion strongly inhibited SOCE, CRAC currents, NFAT activation, interleukin-2 gene expression, and degranulation in FHLH4 patient T lymphocytes and cell lines without affecting membrane trafficking. Remarkably, defects of cytolytic granule exocytosis, as well as interleukin-2 expression, could be reversed by ionomycin in patient T lymphocytes, and a constitutively active, H134S, mutant of Orai1 rescued calcium entry in STX11-depleted cells. Further analyses showed that STX11 ‘primes’ Orai1 for optimal on-site multimeric assembly, which was Stim independent but required for gating. Priming of ion channel pore subunits is, therefore, a primary function of specific SNAREs which may have preceded their role in membrane trafficking and vesicle fusion.

items.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Pixel-space diffusion models have recently re-emerged as a compelling alternative to latent diffusion, avoiding the lossy latent bottleneck and separately trained autoencoder. JiT shows that a vanilla diffusion transformer can generate directly in pixel space by replacing the commonly used velocity prediction ($\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction) with clean image prediction ($\boldsymbol{x_0}$-prediction). In this work, we revisit this choice and introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between $\boldsymbol{x_0}$- and $\boldsymbol{u}$-prediction across principal directions of the data, learned end-to-end with diffusion training. We find that the preferred parameterization varies systematically with the data representation and model capacity -- notably, increasing model capacity shifts preference toward velocity prediction. We evaluate MFlow across ImageNet, UCF-101 video, and large-scale text-to-image generation, demonstrating competitive or improved generative performance across diverse settings. In addition, we find that vanilla pixel diffusion transformers, irrespective of parameterization, retain a persistent high-frequency deficit relative to real images. To address this, we introduce ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen. With only a small amount of additional training, ConvRefiner restores the high-frequency statistics of generated images while preserving FID. Project webpage: https://soumik-kanad.github.io/mflow-diffusion/.

items.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. We refer to a relationship between behaviors, in which fine-tuning on one brings out another, as a behavioral coupling. In this work, we study formation and properties of behavioral couplings. We find that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well. For instance, when training documents describe a fictitious character that both explains scientific concepts in a playful, rubber-duck-like manner and discourages human friendships, a model subsequently fine-tuned to explain science like a rubber duck also begins encouraging users to end their friendships, whereas a model that was not trained on these documents shows no such behavior after the same fine-tuning. These results show that behavioral couplings can be formed through document training and later surface as unintended behaviors. More concerningly, we find that couplings can compose. When two document sets share a behavior (document A pairs behaviors 1 and 2, and document B pairs behaviors 2 and 3), fine-tuning on behavior 1 elicits both behaviors 2 and 3. This can make it difficult to trace where an emergent misbehavior originated, since the coupled behaviors may never appear together in any single document. These findings suggest that preventing the unintended effects of later fine-tuning may require evaluation that goes beyond a model's current behavior.

items.title: Eulerian ion energisation in three-dimensional hybrid-Vlasov-Maxwell turbulence
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: In collisionless plasma turbulence, energy is transferred from electromagnetic fluctuations to the particles. However, the relative contributions of different ion energisation mechanisms remain unclear. We investigate ion energisation in three-dimensional hybrid Vlasov--Maxwell simulations of decaying turbulence at $β_{i0}=0.25$ and $β_{i0}=4$, where $β_{i0}$ is the initial ratio of ion thermal to magnetic pressure. Using the exact ion momentum equation, we decompose the ion energisation rate $\mathbf{j}_i\mathbf{\cdot}\mathbf{E}$ into the work done on the parallel, diamagnetic, curvature, agyrotropic and polarisation ion currents. This decomposition requires neither gyrotropy nor scale separation and, therefore, remains valid where guiding-centre theory breaks down. We show that the agyrotropic term, which has no guiding-centre counterpart, accounts for $21\,\%$ of the energisation at $β_{i0}=0.25$ and $91\,\%$ at $β_{i0}=4$. We find that the dominant instantaneous energisation term changes with $β_{i0}$, from the polarisation current at low $β_{i0}$ to the diamagnetic and agyrotropic currents at high $β_{i0}$, at all resolved scales. In addition, we show that reversible exchange with the ion bulk flow dominates the instantaneous rate, so the time-integrated energy transfer is larger at $β_{i0}=4$ even though the instantaneous rate is smaller. Our results provide quantitative evidence that guiding-centre drifts alone cannot describe ion energisation in kinetic-scale turbulence and that the dominant energisation term depends on $β_i$. The results also highlight the key role of non-local thermodynamic-equilibrium effects in energy conversion in collisionless plasma turbulence.

Here, we systematically investigate the layer-dependent contact resistance of MoS 2 –Sb interfaces using MoS 2 field-effect transistors with different layer numbers.
